subject: Sequenced activation, traffic throttling and acceptance agreement

Subject: Harbor Bank: detailed migration sequencing & throttling mitigation request

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked us to get a detailed migration sequencing plan that also explains how Redwood will handle traffic throttling, burst mitigation, and canary acceptance criteria during the go-live window. Specifically we need: a day-by-day activation timeline, steps for integration (tokenization/schema mapping, auth handoff, telemetry), exact canary gates (latency/error thresholds and rollback triggers), and recommended traffic shaping (percent traffic, rate limits, and warmup).

We need this for the RFI response by end of next week. Would you be able to share a proposed sequence and any sample metric checks we should include in our acceptance tests?

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Soto
Head of Platform Integrations
Harbor Bank

Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 13:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Harbor Bank: detailed migration sequencing & throttling mitigation request

Elena —

Appreciate the clear ask. I've sketched a sequenced activation plan and attached an XLSX that breaks the timeline into pre-launch, canary, ramp, and full activation phases (redwood_migration_sequencing_v1.xlsx). High level summary below — I've kept acceptance gates explicit so you can paste them into your RFI.

Summary (high level):
- Week -4 to -2 (Prep): integration validation (auth, schema, sample traffic), tokenization/embedding mapping verification, secure key exchange and KMS policies, baseline telemetry collection from pre-prod.
- Week -1 (Shadow): shadow traffic at 5% for 72 hours, collect kv-cache hit rates and p50/p95 token latencies, validate end-to-end tracing and logs retention.
- Day 0 (Canary start): route 1%–3% live traffic to Redwood hosted instance. Monitor for 4x sampling of error traces.
- Day 1–3 (Canary expand): if gates pass, increment to 10% over 24–48 hours. If regressions appear, automated fallback to on-prem model variant or previous routing tier.
- Ramp (Day 4–7): increment to 50% then 100% with warmup windows and autoscale checks.

Canary gates (proposed):
- Latency: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 300ms for production-size prompts (10–40 tokens average post-prompt).
- Error rate: user-facing 5xx < 0.2% sustained; spike thresholds defined at >0.5% within 30m.
- Quality regressions: end-to-end BLEU/QA prompt regression < 1.5% vs baseline on our eval set (we can run your critical prompt set in staging).
- Cost delta: per-unit token cost variance vs. expected under 15% during ramp (we'll share batching/quantization knobs).

Traffic shaping / throttling recommendations:
- Warmup: gradual concurrency increase with 10m hold windows; autoscaling policy to add capacity at 70% utilization.
- Rate limits: per-customer burst limit and per-route sustained QPS; recommend 2x burst over baseline with 30s smoothing.
- Backpressure: prefix-level KV cache + client token bucket that returns 429s before queueing to avoid tail latency.

I've routed the XLSX and a short checklist into the shared drive link below. Ben and Markus are on this thread for capacity and SLA detail.

Links: https://redwood.example.com/drive/HB-2027/migration-plan-v1

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions Lead
Redwood Inference

Hi team — quick operational notes to fold into the plan:

- Dedicated capacity: for predictable latency during ramp, we recommend a Dedicated pool pinned for the first 7 days of the canary. That avoids noisy neighbors and simplifies rollback.
- Quantization: if Harbor opts for int8/int4 variants to reduce cost, we'll run a parallel validation on quality prior to canary but expect lower token latency and lower GPU utilization.
- Autoscale policy: recommend aggressive early scale (scale-out threshold 65% GPU util) + conservative scale-in (scale-in threshold 30% util) for the first 48h to avoid oscillation.

I'll add a short section in the spreadsheet about expected GPU minutes per 1k requests at different batch sizes — that's useful for procurement to estimate committed capacity.

-ben
Ben Carter
Head of Field Ops, Redwood Inference

Marissa/Ben —

This is helpful, thank you. A couple of clarifying asks from our side before we finalize the RFI attachment:
1) During the 1% canary window, what exact telemetry streams will you need from our side (traces, user IDs, prompt metadata)? Any PII concerns we should redact?
2) If the error-rate gate trips during the expansion window but latency is fine, what's the standard rollback sequence and expected RTO?
3) We need a short mutual action plan (MAP) with ownership — e.g., Harbor: provide eval prompt set, procurement: PO template; Redwood: provide canary monitoring dashboard and fallback playbook.

Also procurement wants the PO template attached so they can prefill terms. Can you add a short table that maps each canary gate to the artifact or metric we should record?

Thanks — aiming to close the RFI doc by next Wednesday.

-Elena
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@harborbank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Harbor Bank: detailed migration sequencing & throttling mitigation request

Elena —

Answers inline and a short gate->artifact mapping at the bottom.

1) Telemetry: we need anonymized request traces (trace id), request size, prompt family tag, and error codes. PII: do not send raw user PII; instead send pseudonymized IDs or hashed identifiers. We will never store raw prompt text in persistent logs; only sampling for quality checks under NDA.

2) Rollback sequence: automated circuit breaker triggers immediate routing to the previous serving tier (RTO target: under 2 minutes for routing switch; full traffic rollback and verification within 15 minutes). Operations will open a triage channel, run quick root-cause checks (latency, kernel OOM, model mismatch), then either hotfix config or extend rollback.

3) Mutual action plan (short):
- Harbor Bank: supply eval prompt set, fill monitoring contact list, prefill PO template.
- Redwood: provide monitoring dashboard (Grafana + token-level breakdown), canary-runbook, and a test harness to run your eval set in staging.
- Timing: provide PO and eval prompts by EOD Monday to meet the Wednesday RFI cutoff.

Gate -> artifact mapping:
- Latency gate: p50/p95 time series (Grafana panel) + sample traces for 5 failing requests.
- Error-rate gate: 5xx time series + trace ids for 100 sampled failures.
- Quality gate: eval run results CSV (baseline vs canary) + example regenerations for flagged prompts.
- Cost gate: cost per 1k tokens estimate (spreadsheet) and actualized cost snapshot at 24h.

I attached a short PO template (harbor_po_template.docx) in the shared link and added the gate table to the XLSX.

-Markus
